court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
case_name: Amit Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. And Others

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a writ petition seeking quashing of the First Information Report No.1049/2019 against him under various IPC sections and Dowry Prohibition Act. He also sought an order directing the respondents not to arrest him.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal proceedings can be quashed by the court on the basis of mutual settlement.
legal_principles.held: Considering the compromise arrived at between the parties, we are of the considered opinion that no useful purpose would be served in continuation of criminal proceedings.
cited_cases: Dinesh Sharma and Ors. Vs. State of U.P and Ors., (2017) ADJ 613

legal_principles.principle: The court should accept the terms of a compromise in criminal proceedings where the question involved is of a purely personal nature.
legal_principles.held: We need to emphasise that it is perhaps advisable that in disputes where the question involved is of a purely personal nature, the court should ordinarily accept the terms of the compromise even in criminal proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: Technicalities should not be allowed to stand in the way of quashing criminal proceedings where there is a compromise between parties.
legal_principles.held: Although the power should be used by the court sparingly, technicality should not be allowed to stand in the way of quashing criminal proceeding.
cited_cases: Shiji @ Pappu and Ors. Vs. Radhika and another, (2011) CJ (SC) 239

outcome.final_order: The Court allowed the writ petition and quashed the First Information Report.
